info.name: classifier
info.description:
Document Classifier — JPEG/PNG photos, PDFs of any page count, SVG drawings, .txt and .docx, several documents per request, scored by OpenCV detectors, deterministic text matching, the open-vocabulary detector, and vision-LLM criteria — called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/classifier` → `http://classifier:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE, `forward_headers: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key: set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/classifier/API.md for the full reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing keys.

Direct base URL (bypassing LiteLLM, only inside ai_shared or when PORT_CLASSIFIER is published): http://classifier:8000 or http://<host>:${PORT_CLASSIFIER} — no auth there.

ONE analysis endpoint: POST /assess, as JSON (`{documents: [{type: base64|url|text, data}, …], criteria}` — or `{document: {…}}` for one; not both) or multipart (repeated `file` parts and/or `text` fields, plus `criteria` once). `/locate` and `/assess/compare` were removed (404); `/locate`'s job is `score: false` on a criterion. A criterion is `{name, type, weight, depends_on, score, options}` with the type-specific settings in `options` — GET /criterion-types has each type's schema, defaults and caps. Every page of every document is one ITEM (at most CLASSIFIER_MAX_ITEMS = 20 per request, counted at submit; 21 is a 400 with a per-document breakdown); each criterion runs once per item and `options.aggregate` collapses the per-item results — pages → per document → per request (API.md § Documents, pages and items). An SVG is one item rendered by MuPDF, which never fetches what it links to: each external reference is a line in the result's `documents[].warnings` — or, with CLASSIFIER_SVG_FETCH_IMAGES on, `<image>` links are fetched AT SUBMIT through the SSRF guard and inlined (API.md § External references in SVG).

Async-job pattern: POST /assess returns 202 with `{job_id, phase: "pending"}`; poll GET /jobs/:jobId until `phase` is `completed` or `failed`. The SQLite jobs table is the queue: CLASSIFIER_MAX_CONCURRENT (default 4) jobs at once; inside a job CLASSIFIER_MAX_UNITS_PER_JOB (2) (criterion, item) units at once; CLASSIFIER_MAX_LLM_CALLS (4) model calls and CLASSIFIER_OCR_WORKERS (4) OCR passes across the whole process. Copy a `job_id` into the `jobId` collection variable to run the GET/DELETE items.

Artifacts: every job stores regions.json, one text.p<n>.<key>.json per item and text layer its criteria used (text.d<i>.<key>.json for a scope-document text search), one p<n>.base.jpg per item with an image, and a manifest with the item map; SVG / PNG / preview layers (p<n>.*) render on first fetch. See the Artifacts folder.

Folders: `Documents` (one request per fixture in unit-tests/classifier/documents/, plus a two-page PDF and a three-document request), `Regions` (fixtures chosen for their geometry), `Documents + regions` (the document fixtures again, geometry-focused), `Artifacts` (the four artifact routes), `References` (saved worked examples — POST, list, read, files, PATCH, DELETE). `unit-tests/classifier/regions_report.py` runs the first three as a suite (REGIONS_REPORT.md).

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). The pass-through runs with `auth: true`, so a non-admin virtual key needs `/v1/classifier` in its (or its team's) `metadata.allowed_passthrough_routes` — set under `metadata`, by a proxy admin, because the top-level field is Enterprise-only; the master key works without it. Otherwise 403. See ai/litellm/LITELLM.md § Pass-through auth. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth, then forwarded to the classifier by LiteLLM because the pass-through has `forward_headers: true`.

job_id returned by POST /assess. Fill in after submitting to run GET /jobs/:jobId, DELETE /jobs/:jobId, and every request in the Artifacts folder. `phase` values progress staging → pending → processing → completed | failed.

A file name in the job's artifact directory — see GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts for the list. n is the job's global ITEM index (every page of every document; the manifest's `items` map says which document and page n is). Written at job time: `regions.json`, `manifest.json`, `p<n>.base.jpg` (per item with a page image), one `text.p<n>.<key>.json` per item and distinct text layer the criteria used (`text.p0.auto.json`, `text.p0.always.json`, `text.p1.never.json`, …), and `text.d<i>.<key>.json` for a scope-document text search. Rendered on FIRST FETCH and then cached: `p<n>.svg`, `p<n>.layer.png`, `p<n>.preview.jpg`, and per criterion `p<n>.<slug>.svg` / `.layer.png` / `.preview.jpg`. Always available as a view: `text.p<n>.<key>.txt` / `text.d<i>.<key>.txt` (the layer's text, plain).

Base64 of unit-tests/classifier/documents/invoice_native.pdf, WITHOUT a data: prefix, for the JSON-body items. Fill it once: `base64 -w0 unit-tests/classifier/documents/invoice_native.pdf` (macOS: `base64 -i … | tr -d '\n'`; PowerShell: [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('…'))) and paste the output into this variable's CURRENT VALUE.
reference_id returned by POST /references (`r` + 12 hex). Fill in to run the References folder's GET / PATCH / DELETE items and the /assess items that list a reference.
A reference file name: page.jpg, working.jpg, c.<slug>.jpg (GET /references/:referenceId lists them), regions.json or record.json.

request.description: Liveness check used by the Docker healthcheck. Returns `{"status": "ok"}`. Excluded from the Prometheus request metrics.

Every criterion type's options, for THIS container: `types.<llm|text|cv|detector>` carries `options_schema` (JSON schema generated from the same pydantic model POST /assess validates against — `additionalProperties: false`, so an unknown key is a 400), `defaults` (resolved: `text.pattern` shows `<name>` because it defaults to the criterion name; `cv.fallback` is `detector` when DETECTOR_URL is configured, else `llm`) and `caps` (server limits a request may not exceed, e.g. `llm.max_attempts` = CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS). Also `shared_fields` (name, type, weight, depends_on, score) and `detector_configured`. No errors. See API.md § `GET /criterion-types`. Also carries `aggregate`: the two levels (pages → per document, documents → per request), what each rule means (`any`, `worst`, `all` = alias of worst, `mean`, `sum` — text only), and the defaults table (llm presence / detector: any + all; llm quality / auto, cv: worst + worst; text: sum + sum). Each type's `defaults` include its resolved `aggregate` (and `scope` for text). Each type also carries `result`: the shape of the `detail` it returns — `metric` (the headline number: `score` for llm, `count` for text, `best_score` for detector, per detector for cv), `metric_from` (`score` | `detail` | `measurements`), and `fields` (every detail key with its JSON `kind`, a `description`, `when` it appears if not always, and `stable` if it survives a `mean` aggregate). The top-level `aggregate_detail` describes the `{rule, level, from, values}` block an aggregated detail gains. cv measurement keys per detector: GET /cv-detectors. See API.md § Result details.

Every `options.hint` value an `llm` criterion may carry (`quality`, `presence`, `auto`) and the rubric text the model is given for each — the table is `config.HINT_RUBRICS`, verbatim. A `cv` criterion that falls back to the llm uses `auto`. No errors. See API.md § `GET /hints`.

Every registered OpenCV detector name, grouped by the function behind it — the names a `type: "cv"` criterion is matched against (exact, then difflib at CV_NAME_FUZZY_CUTOFF 0.8). A name that matches none uses the criterion's `options.fallback`. Returns `{detectors: [{function, names, technique, metric, measurements, thresholds, parameters, states, regions}], total_names}` — each detector's aliases plus the shape of the `detail` it returns: `metric` (the headline key), `measurements` (every key, each `{unit, description}`; units `ratio` 0-1, `px` working-image pixels, `count`, `variance`, `intensity` 0-255), `thresholds` (key → what it decides), `parameters` (keys), `states` (value → meaning; `{}` when the detector has none) and `regions` (what its regions are, or null). Test-checked against the detectors' real output. No errors. See API.md § `GET /cv-detectors`.

What this container accepts and how it is handled right now: the five kinds (image, svg and .txt/.docx one item each, pdf one item PER PAGE — the svg entry's `external_images` is the live CLASSIFIER_SVG_FETCH_* setting), the refused legacy .doc and .svgz, the accepted inputs (JSON `documents: [base64 | url | text, …]` or the one-`document` shorthand; multipart repeatable `file` | `text`), the text-match modes, the live OCR status (`ocr.available` loads the engine to answer honestly), the limits (`max_items` = CLASSIFIER_MAX_ITEMS, render DPI, `svg_max_render_pixels`, the LLM text budget, and the four concurrency limits: jobs, units per job, model calls, OCR passes), and the regions block (always stored; layers render on first fetch; the llm box-loop bounds; the live detector status; `artifact_max_bytes_per_item`). No errors.

formdata.description: A document: JPEG, PNG, PDF (every page is an item), SVG, .txt or .docx. REPEAT the part for more documents — this item sends two. The kind is detected from the bytes (common.documents.detect_kind), never from the filename or Content-Type. The `src` points at a repo fixture — re-select the file if your Postman working directory differs. The legacy part name `image` is also accepted, and repeats too.
A second document, as a repeated `file` part: one more item. Parts are taken in form order.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes, sent ONCE: it covers every document. See GET /criterion-types.

request.description:
Submit an assessment job — the one analysis endpoint. This item is the multipart form of it: repeated `file` parts (the legacy name `image` is still accepted) and/or repeated `text` fields — each one a document, in form order — plus ONE `criteria` field holding a JSON array. The JSON items below send the SAME request as a body; both are parsed into one `AssessRequest`, so they cannot behave differently. Returns **202 Accepted** with `{"job_id", "phase": "pending"}`; poll GET /jobs/:jobId.

**Items.** Every page of every document is one item — this request is invoice_native.pdf (1 page) + photo_of_letter.png = 2 items. At most CLASSIFIER_MAX_ITEMS (20) per request, INCLUSIVE, counted at submit from the bytes (a PDF's page count without rendering); 21 is a 400 naming each document's pages: `too many items: 21 pages across 11 document(s) exceeds CLASSIFIER_MAX_ITEMS=20 (#0 a.pdf: 2 pages, …)`.

A criterion is `{name, type, weight, depends_on, score, options}` — only the shared fields at the top, everything type-specific in `options` (GET /criterion-types has the schema, defaults and caps):
  llm: `hint` (quality | presence | auto), `boxes` (default false — the bounding-box loop), `max_attempts` (≤ CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS), `ocr` (auto | always | never — the text layer sent with the prompt), `aggregate`
  text: `pattern` (default: the name), `match` (contains | exact | regex | fuzzy), `case_sensitive`, `fuzzy_threshold`, `min_count`, `ocr`, `scope` (page | document — document joins a document's pages with one space so a phrase over a page break matches), `aggregate`
  cv: `fallback` (detector | llm — what answers when no OpenCV detector matches; default detector when DETECTOR_URL is set, else llm), `aggregate`
  detector: `threshold` (default DETECTOR_MIN_SCORE), `aggregate`
`aggregate` (every type): a rule for both levels, or `{pages, documents}` — `any` (best item), `worst` / `all` (lowest item; all is an alias), `mean`, `sum` (text only: hit counts added). Defaults: llm presence / detector any + all; llm quality / auto, cv worst + worst; text sum + sum. Skipped and errored units are excluded; any errored unit makes the criterion incomplete.
`score: false` locates without judging (regions, no score/verdict, excluded from the weighting) — /locate's old job. `depends_on` names another SCORED criterion that must PASS first, gated PER ITEM: the dependant runs on the items where its dependency passed and is SKIPPED (no model call) on the others.

The unit of work is (criterion, item): one `llm` unit = one model call; up to CLASSIFIER_MAX_UNITS_PER_JOB units run at once; model calls across all jobs are bounded by CLASSIFIER_MAX_LLM_CALLS and OCR passes by CLASSIFIER_OCR_WORKERS. OCR is memoised per item by settings — criteria with the same `ocr` share one pass per page. A unit that fails (model down, unparseable answer, detector outage) gets `status: "error"` alone; the job still completes.

**Errors (400 at submit, nothing queued):** unknown / mistyped / over-cap option (named, e.g. `criteria.0: options.max_attempts: max_attempts 9 exceeds this server's cap…`), an `aggregate` that is not a rule or `{pages, documents}`, `sum` on a non-text criterion, an old top-level key (`hint`, `pattern`, … — 'moved into options'), an invalid regex, duplicate names, unknown `depends_on`, a dependency on a `score: false` criterion, a dependency cycle, `score: false` on a criterion that cannot produce geometry or when no document has a page image, a `detector` criterion when DETECTOR_URL is unset, a removed form field (`ocr`, `regions`), no `file` / `text` at all, an empty `text` field, `criteria` sent twice, an unsupported kind (named by document — legacy .doc → convert to .docx), and **more than CLASSIFIER_MAX_ITEMS items**. **415** for a Content-Type that is neither JSON nor multipart. **500** if the payload could not be persisted. `/locate` and `/assess/compare` no longer exist and answer 404.

Result shape (GET /jobs/:jobId → `result`, `schema_version: 3`):
  `{schema_version, documents, items, assessment: {overall_score, overall_verdict, complete, weighted_score_breakdown, per_criterion_scores}, verdict, page_geometry, detector, artifacts}`
Every page of every document is one ITEM, numbered globally in request order. `documents[]` is `{index, filename, kind, pages, items, document_info}` (document_info: content_type, size_bytes, has_image, native_text_chars, ocr.layers per item, ocr.document_layers, llm_text_char_budget). `items[]` is `{item, document, page, filename, overall_score, overall_verdict, complete}` — each item's own weighted score. `page_geometry` is a list, one entry per item (null sizes for a .txt/.docx item); `page` there, a region's `page` and the `p{n}` layer prefix all mean the item.
Every entry of `per_criterion_scores` has the SAME keys — the AGGREGATED answer: `status` (ok | error | skipped), `type`, `method`, `scored`, `score`, `verdict`, `confidence`, `reason`, `detail`, `regions` (the union over every item, capped at CLASSIFIER_INLINE_REGIONS_MAX with `regions_truncated`), `artifacts` (`items`: per item, that page's layer URLs filtered to the criterion and its loop `attempts`; `text`: one link per text layer its units read), `localization` (llm: the loop's record — merged across items), `options_used` (with `aggregate` resolved), `error`, `complete` (false when any of its units errored), `aggregate_used` ({pages, documents}), and `items` — one entry per unit: `{item, document, page, status, score, verdict, confidence, reason, detail, error, regions (a COUNT), text_layer, localization (llm)}`.
The overall score and verdict are weighed over the AGGREGATED criterion results; `complete` is false when any scored criterion is incomplete, and `overall_score` / `overall_verdict` are then null with the partial score in `weighted_score_breakdown` (`partial: true`). `score: false`, skipped and errored criteria never count toward the score.

See API.md § `POST /assess` and § Documents, pages and items.

The same request as the multipart POST /assess, as a JSON body: `{"documents": [{"type": "base64", "data": "…", "filename": "…"}], "criteria": [...]}` — a one-item `documents` list. `filename` is optional and only recorded in `documents[i].filename`. Fill the `invoice_native_b64` collection variable first (see its description). Returns 202 with a job_id. Same errors as POST /assess, plus 400 for invalid base64, both `document` and `documents`, or a body that is not a JSON object. See API.md § Request.

`type: "url"` — the service fetches the URL AT SUBMIT (the item cap needs the bytes: a PDF counts its pages), after the SSRF check (common.net: private, loopback and link-local addresses are refused). This item uses the one-document shorthand `{"document": {…}}`, which is a one-item `documents` list — sending both keys is a 400. Returns 202. **400** for a blocked or unresolvable URL, **502** when the fetch fails, plus every POST /assess 400. Replace the example URL with a real document.

`type: "text"` — the document IS the string, treated as a .txt (UTF-8), one item. No page image, so `cv` / `detector` units are SKIPPED, `score: false` is refused (no document in the request has an image), and the llm prompt is text-only. `documents[0].filename` is `inline.txt`. Returns 202. Errors as POST /assess.

formdata.value: NOTICE TO OWNER — Under Florida law, those who work on your property…
formdata.description: Inline text, treated as a .txt document (one item). Repeatable, and may be mixed with `file` parts — each is one document.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes, sent ONCE: it covers every document. See GET /criterion-types.

request.description: The multipart spelling of inline text: a `text` form field instead of (or alongside) a `file` part. Parsed into the same AssessRequest as the JSON `type: "text"` document, so the two produce identical results. Returns 202. **400** when there is no `file` / `text` at all, or a `text` field is empty.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, documents list (a PDF, a URL and inline text)

request.description:
Several documents in ONE job: `documents` is a list, each entry `{type: base64 | url | text, data, filename?}`, in order. Every page of every document is one item — here invoice_native.pdf (1 page) + the URL's document + the inline text = 3 items, when the URL is an image or a one-page PDF. Fill `invoice_native_b64` and replace the example URL first.

Each criterion runs once per item and is aggregated: `Notice to Owner` uses the text default (`sum`: hit counts added across items and documents, so ONE hit anywhere passes); `Notice to Owner in every document` keeps the `sum` pages rule but sets `documents: all` (= worst), so every document must have it; `has a signature` is PASS if any page of any document shows one; `sharpness` (cv: worst / worst) is skipped on the text item and excluded, so the worst of the two images decides. Each result entry's `items` lists the per-item answers, and the top-level `items` the per-item scores. Returns 202; same errors as POST /assess (a document is named `#<index> <filename>` in its error). See API.md § Documents, pages and items.

item.name: POST /assess — multipart, repeated files and text fields

formdata.description: Document 0 — a two-page PDF: items 0 and 1.
Document 1 — a repeated `file` part: item 2.
Document 2 — inline text, a repeatable field: item 3.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes, sent ONCE: it covers every document. See GET /criterion-types.

request.description:
Repeated multipart parts: two `file` parts and a `text` field are three documents and FOUR items (the PDF has two pages). The service takes them in form order — note that some clients (httpx `files=` / `data=`, requests) send every plain field before every file, which makes the inline text document 0; the result's `documents` / `items` say which is which.

`Net 30` (text, sum): found on the PDF's page 2 and in the text → PASS, `detail.count` 2, `detail.counts` per document. `Net 30 on every page` (`aggregate: "all"` at both levels) → FAIL: page 1 of the PDF and the photo do not have it. `has text` (`score: false`) returns block boxes on the PDF pages and the photo, each region with its item as `page`. Returns 202. See API.md § Documents, pages and items.

Guide llm criteria with stored examples. Each llm-answered criterion is matched by name (case-insensitive, or `options.reference.criterion`) to the listed references' usable criteria; with a PASS and a FAIL example the scoring call is ONE contrastive call with three images (example, counter-example, candidate). `options.reference`: use, criterion, position (off | check — needs boxes; a miss caps the score), min_iou, combine (any | all | mean). The answer is in each unit's `detail.reference` and the result's top-level `references`; the job writes references.json. Errors: 400 for every reference rule (no references with options.reference, options.reference on text / detector / OpenCV cv, unknown ids, more than CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_MAX_PER_CRITERION examples, position check vs a whole-page example, …); 409 a reference not ready. Set `referenceId` first. See API.md § References.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, criteria inherited from references

request.description: `criteria` omitted with explicit reference ids → the references' own criteria, merged by name in list order (a name defined differently in two references is a 400 naming both). The result's `request.criteria` shows what ran and `references.inherited` is true. Without references an omitted `criteria` still means the four default quality criteria.

item.name: POST /assess — JSON, references auto with tags

request.description: Let the service pick examples: the pool is fixed at submit (ready references with a usable criterion matching one of these criteria, carrying all / any of the tags, newest first, at most CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_AUTO_POOL_MAX); each page item then makes ONE selection call (the page as its one image plus a text catalogue of the pool), and each criterion keeps the matches at or above CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_AUTO_MIN_CONFIDENCE. A failed selection only degrades — the error is in `references.selection`. `criteria` is required (400 without).

List jobs, newest first (common.jobs.router). Query `phase` filters by phase, `limit` (default 50) caps the page. Each row is `{job_id, phase, created_at, updated_at, elapsed_seconds, metadata: {type, request_id}, result, error}` — `metadata.type` is always `assess` (rows queued by an older container may say `compare` / `locate`; those fail with a message naming the removed type). Results can be large — prefer GET /jobs/:jobId.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

request.description:
Poll one job. `phase` progresses staging → pending → processing → completed | failed. When `completed`, `result` is the assessment:

Result shape (GET /jobs/:jobId → `result`, `schema_version: 3`):
  `{schema_version, documents, items, assessment: {overall_score, overall_verdict, complete, weighted_score_breakdown, per_criterion_scores}, verdict, page_geometry, detector, artifacts, references, request, usage}`
Every page of every document is one ITEM, numbered globally in request order. `documents[]` is `{index, filename, kind, pages, items, document_info}` (document_info: content_type, size_bytes, has_image, native_text_chars, ocr.layers per item, ocr.document_layers, llm_text_char_budget). `items[]` is `{item, document, page, filename, overall_score, overall_verdict, complete}` — each item's own weighted score. `page_geometry` is a list, one entry per item (null sizes for a .txt/.docx item); `page` there, a region's `page` and the `p{n}` layer prefix all mean the item.
Every entry of `per_criterion_scores` has the SAME keys — the AGGREGATED answer: `status` (ok | error | skipped), `type`, `method`, `scored`, `score`, `verdict`, `confidence`, `reason`, `detail`, `regions` (the union over every item, capped at CLASSIFIER_INLINE_REGIONS_MAX with `regions_truncated`), `artifacts` (`items`: per item, that page's layer URLs filtered to the criterion and its loop `attempts`; `text`: one link per text layer its units read), `localization` (llm: the loop's record — merged across items), `options_used` (with `aggregate` resolved), `error`, `complete` (false when any of its units errored), `aggregate_used` ({pages, documents}), and `items` — one entry per unit: `{item, document, page, status, score, verdict, confidence, reason, detail, error, regions (a COUNT), text_layer, localization (llm)}`.
The overall score and verdict are weighed over the AGGREGATED criterion results; `complete` is false when any scored criterion is incomplete, and `overall_score` / `overall_verdict` are then null with the partial score in `weighted_score_breakdown` (`partial: true`). `score: false`, skipped and errored criteria never count toward the score.
`usage` is what the job's vision-model requests cost: `{calls, errors, seconds, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_tokens, models, first_call_at, last_call_at, usage_url}` — the per-call rows are at GET /jobs/:jobId/usage.

A model outage does NOT fail the job — it fails the unit (`status: "error"` on that item) and the job completes with `complete: false`. `failed` means the job itself could not run (a thumbnail-sized page image, an undecodable file, a payload from an older container — anything but `schema: 3`). **404** for an unknown job id. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

request.description: Delete the job row, its artifact directory AND its model-usage rows (the router's `on_delete` hook removes the directory and the `llm_calls` rows first, so nothing is left that nothing points at — the `text.*.json` layers go with it). **404** for an unknown job id — but the hook runs before that check, so a DELETE on a job the TTL sweeper already removed still deletes its usage rows (the one thing the sweeper leaves behind). A running job is not interrupted. See API.md § `DELETE /jobs/{job_id}`.

item.name: References
item.description: Saved worked examples (API.md § References). A reference is ONE page — a JPEG/PNG, or one page of a PDF — with the criteria asked of it, the answer each should get and where the feature is; an /assess that lists it shows the vision model the example beside the candidate. LLM-only: llm criteria and cv names answered by the llm fallback. Creating one runs a `reference` job (visible in GET /jobs); poll GET /references/:referenceId until `status` is ready or failed. Kept until DELETE — never swept. PATCH needs `PATCH` in the LiteLLM /v1/classifier pass-through's methods.

request.description: Save a worked example from a document. `breakdown` is the answer key (`verdict` optional, must match the score); `regions` says where (`[]` = the whole page; a name left out is located by the creation job); `region_units` px (original page pixels) or grid (0-1000, recommended for PDFs). `a roof` has no breakdown, so the creation job classifies it, and — presence, no regions — locates it with boxes forced on. `description` omitted → generated by one model call (CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_DESCRIBE). Returns 202 `{reference_id, status: "pending", job_id}`. Errors: 400 for any malformed input (a .txt / .docx, a page the PDF does not have, a region off the page, a verdict that disagrees with its score, a breakdown / regions key naming no criterion, grid coordinates past 1000); 409 at CLASSIFIER_REFERENCE_MAX_COUNT. Fill `invoice_native_b64` or swap in your own base64 image. See API.md § References — Creating one.

formdata.description: The example page.
JSON array — the same CriterionInput list /assess takes.

formdata.value: {"has a house": {"score": 10, "reason": "two-storey houses along the street"}}
formdata.description: {name: {score, verdict?, reason?}}
[] = the whole page is the example.

formdata.value: A residential street of detached houses seen from above.

item.name: Artifacts
item.description: The four artifact routes, plus the text-layer view. Every job writes an artifact directory (regions.json, text.p<n>.<key>.json per item and text layer, text.d<i>.<key>.json for a scope-document search, p<n>.base.jpg per item with an image, manifest.json with the `items` map); layers render on first fetch. n is the global item index. Set `jobId` (and `artifactName`) from a completed job.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

query.description: Criterion SLUG (not name), from the manifest's `criteria` map or a result's `artifacts.slug`. Repeatable — the union of the criteria given. Scopes the manifest: `files` whose `criteria` intersect them, only those `criteria` entries, only the `items` they have regions on or read a text layer for, plus `layers` and `filter`. An unknown slug is a 400.

request.description:
The manifest: `{job_id, created_at, expires_at, options, criteria, page_geometry, files, total_bytes, dropped, notes, items, zip_url}`. `files` is what is on disk NOW, each with its `url` — layers appear once they have been fetched (they render on first fetch). Every `files` entry is labelled: `kind` (`manifest` | `regions` | `text` | `layer` | `base`; `other` never occurs for a name the service writes), `format` where it adds information (layers `svg` | `png` | `preview`, text layers `json`; omitted otherwise), `item` (the global item index, `null` for manifest.json, regions.json and document-scope `text.d<i>.*`), `document` (from the `items` map, `i` for `text.d<i>.*`, `null` for job-wide files) and `criteria` (sorted criterion NAMES the file belongs to: every criterion for manifest.json / regions.json; the criteria that read a text layer; every criterion with a region on item n for `p<n>.svg|layer.png|preview.jpg` and `p<n>.base.jpg`; exactly the one criterion for `p<n>.<slug>.*`). The job result's `artifacts.files` carries the same labels (one function writes both). `criteria` maps each criterion name to its `slug`, region `count`, `sources`, and `text_layers` (the `text.p<n>.<key>.json` / `text.d<i>.<key>.json` files its units used). `items` maps each item n to `{document, page, filename}`; `options.byte_cap` is `{per_item, items, total}` — CLASSIFIER_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES is a per-item allowance.

**`?criterion=<slug>` (repeatable)** scopes it to those criteria: `files`, `criteria` and `items` cut down as above (`total_bytes` is the scoped files' sum), `layers` — `{"<n>": {"<slug>": {svg, png, preview}}}`, on each item where that criterion has hits (regions) only — a page it searched without a hit is in `items` but gets no layer — the URLs `p<n>.svg?criterion=<slug>` / `p<n>.layer.png?criterion=<slug>` / `p<n>.preview.jpg?criterion=<slug>` (preview only when `p<n>.base.jpg` exists), fetchable whether or not they are rendered yet — `filter: {criterion: [slugs], criteria: [names]}`, and `zip_url` carrying the same `?criterion=`. Without it the manifest is the whole job.

Every job writes a directory, so **404** means the job is unknown or has not finished; **410** means it had artifacts and the TTL sweeper or a DELETE removed them; **400** for an unknown slug. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts`.

query.description: Criterion SLUG (not name), from the manifest's `criteria` map or a result's `artifacts.slug`. Repeatable. Filters the render to that criterion's regions. An unknown slug is a 400.
Comma list of `cv`, `ocr`, `pdf-text`, `llm`, `detector`. Only regions from those sources are drawn.
LLM criteria only: the box from enforcement-loop attempt N, accepted or not — how a REJECTED box is viewed on its own. `artifacts.attempts[]` in the result carries these URLs ready-made.
LLM criteria only. `true` (the default when no `attempt` is given) keeps the accepted attempt; `false` keeps the rejected ones.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

A file name in the job's artifact directory — see GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts for the list. n is the job's global ITEM index (every page of every document; the manifest's `items` map says which document and page n is). Written at job time: `regions.json`, `manifest.json`, `p<n>.base.jpg` (per item with a page image), one `text.p<n>.<key>.json` per item and distinct text layer the criteria used (`text.p0.auto.json`, `text.p0.always.json`, `text.p1.never.json`, …), and `text.d<i>.<key>.json` for a scope-document text search. Rendered on FIRST FETCH and then cached: `p<n>.svg`, `p<n>.layer.png`, `p<n>.preview.jpg`, and per criterion `p<n>.<slug>.svg` / `.layer.png` / `.preview.jpg`. Always available as a view: `text.p<n>.<key>.txt` / `text.d<i>.<key>.txt` (the layer's text, plain).

request.description:
Stream one file with its content type (`application/json`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`). n is the job's global item index.

* A file that exists is streamed as-is.
* A LAYER that does not exist yet — `p<n>.svg`, `p<n>.layer.png`, `p<n>.preview.jpg`, or per criterion `p<n>.<slug>.svg|layer.png|preview.jpg` — is rendered from `regions.json` now and cached into the directory (counting against the job's byte cap: CLASSIFIER_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES × its items).
* With any query filter (`criterion`, `source`, `attempt`, `accepted`) `regions.json` or a combined `p<n>.*` layer is re-rendered for that subset by the same renderer; only the plain single-criterion view is cached (as `p<n>.<slug>.<suffix>`), so the filtered and stored views can never disagree. An `attempt` number is per item — each item's unit runs its own loop.
* `text.p<n>.<key>.txt` / `text.d<i>.<key>.txt` returns the `text` field of the matching `.json` as plain text.

**Errors:** 400 for an unsafe name, an unknown slug, or a filter on a file that is not regions.json / a combined layer; 404 for an unknown or unfinished job, a missing file that is not a layer, a layer on an item with no page image (.txt/.docx) or no such item, or a preview whose base image the byte cap dropped; 410 when the directory was swept or deleted. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts/{name}`.

item.name: GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts/:artifactName — text.p0.auto.json (the text a criterion searched)

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

`text.p<n>.<key>.json` — item n's layer under a setting; the file is in each unit's `items[].text_layer.url` and in the criterion's `artifacts.text[].url` (and the manifest's `criteria.<name>.text_layers`). `text.d<i>.<key>.json` for a scope-document search. Swap `.json` for `.txt` for plain text.

request.description:
The exact text a `text` unit searched (and an `llm` unit was sent), as the job stored it. One file per ITEM and distinct text layer, named `text.p<n>.<key>.json` — the key is the settings: `auto`, `always`, `never` (a future non-default OCR setting adds a hash: `auto-1a2b3c4d`) — and shared by every criterion that used those settings on that page. Each unit's entry links its own (`items[].text_layer = {key, url, source, chars}`), the criterion lists them all (`artifacts.text = [{item, key, url, source, chars}, …]`), and `options_used.ocr` agrees with the key.

Body: `{key, item, settings: {mode, min_native_chars, engine}, source: native|ocr|none, engine: "rapidocr"|null, chars, confidence, text, lines: [{text, polygon, confidence}]}`. `text` is byte-for-byte the string `match_text` searched, so a failed match can be diagnosed from this file alone. `lines` are the OCR lines with polygons in ORIGINAL page pixels; empty for native text (.txt, .docx, and native PDF text, whose line geometry is not recorded).

A text criterion with `options.scope: "document"` searched `text.d<i>.<key>.json` instead: `{key, scope: "document", document, settings, separator: " ", source, chars, text, segments: [{item, page, start, end, page_offset, file}]}` — the document's pages' layers joined in page order, and where each page sits in the joined string.

Set `artifactName` to `text.p0.auto.txt` for the same text as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`. Written for every job whose criteria read text, native or OCR'd; never dropped by the byte cap; deleted with the job. **404** when the job has no layer by that name.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

query.description: Criterion SLUG (not name). Repeatable — the union. Scopes the zip to what belongs to those criteria (see the item description). An unknown slug is a 400.

request.description:
Every file currently in the directory, streamed as one zip (`application/zip`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`), each entry `<job_id>/<name>`. Built from what is on disk, so layers that were never fetched are not in it — fetch them first if you want them.

**`?criterion=<slug>` (repeatable)** streams ONLY what belongs to those criteria: `regions.json` reduced to them and the scoped `manifest.json` (as the manifest's `?criterion=` returns it) — both generated for the zip, the stored files are never rewritten — the text layers they read, the `p<n>.base.jpg` of each item they have regions on, and each criterion's own `p<n>.<slug>.svg` / `.layer.png` / `.preview.jpg` on those items, rendered and cached first if nobody has fetched them (preview only where the base exists). Combined `p<n>.*` layers are not included. A byte-capped directory yields what survived. The manifest's file labels are described on GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts.

**404** / **410** as for the manifest; **400** for an unknown slug. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts.zip`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`.

request.description: Free the disk and keep the job row: removes the whole artifact directory (regions.json, text layers, base image, cached layers). **204** on success; **404** for an unknown job or one with no directory. Afterwards the artifact routes answer **410**. The inline regions in the result survive.

item.name: Usage
item.description: What each job's vision-model requests cost. Every HTTP request to VISION_LLM_API is one row of the `llm_calls` table in the classifier-db Postgres (also readable from Trino as postgres_classifier.public.llm_calls), linked to its job, criterion and item; the rows outlive the job's TTL and go only with DELETE /jobs/:jobId. A completed job's result carries the totals as `usage`. Set `jobId` from a POST /assess or POST /references response. See API.md § Model usage.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess (202 body). Paste it here, or set the collection variable `jobId`. An expired job's id still works here — the usage rows outlive the job.

request.description:
Every vision-model HTTP request the job made — each scoring call, box-loop ask / refine / verify, `references: "auto"` selection, reference description, and each parse retry, failed requests included — with its totals. Returns `{job_id, job_present, job_type, totals, by_kind, by_outcome, by_criterion, calls}`.

`totals` is `{calls, errors, seconds, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_tokens, models, first_call_at, last_call_at}` — the same block the job result carries as `usage` (plus `usage_url` there). A token total is `null`, not 0, when no call reported it (`cached_tokens` needs `--enable-prompt-tokens-details` on muse-glimmer). `by_kind` (score | ask | refine | verify | select | describe | other) and `by_outcome` (ok | error) map to the same block; `by_criterion` is a LIST of blocks each with its `criterion` — `null` for the calls that belong to no criterion (the per-item selection, a reference's description).

`calls[]`, in the order made: `{id, job_id, job_type, request_id, started_at, label, kind, criterion, item, document, attempt, model_requested, model_reported, api_url, max_tokens, outcome, http_status, error, finish_reason, seconds, prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens, reasoning_tokens, total_tokens, usage}` — `usage` is the response's raw `usage` object; `seconds` is time inside the CLASSIFIER_MAX_LLM_CALLS slot (the model, not the wait); `http_status` / `error` are set on a failed request.

**200** with zero calls for a job that has not called the model (queued, or text / cv criteria only). **200 with `job_present: false`** once the TTL sweeper has removed the job — the usage rows outlive it. **404** only when there is neither a job row nor any usage row (an unknown id, or a job removed with DELETE /jobs/:jobId). See API.md § Model usage and § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/usage`.

query.description: Inclusive lower bound on a call's `started_at`: an ISO date (its midnight UTC) or datetime (`2026-10-01T08:00:00Z`; no offset means UTC).
Exclusive upper bound, same forms. `since=2026-10-01&until=2026-10-02` is one UTC day. Must be after `since`.
Only calls made by jobs of this type: assess | reference.

request.description: Model usage across jobs, expired ones included (the usage rows outlive their jobs). request.description: What /locate used to do. Both criteria have `score: false`: they run exactly as scored ones and return their regions, but `score` / `verdict` / `confidence` are null and they are excluded from the weighting — so `overall_score` and `verdict` are null and `weighted_score_breakdown` is null. Expected: `has text` 4 boxes, `Notice to Owner` ≥ 1 `ocr` polygon. `score: false` on a criterion that cannot produce geometry (an llm criterion without `options.boxes`, `sharpness`) is a 400.

formdata.description: The document. Its kind is detected from the bytes, never the filename or the part's Content-Type.
JSON array of criterion objects — the same shape the JSON body's `criteria` takes. See GET /criterion-types.

request.description: The loop runs per criterion with `options.boxes: true`: ask for a box on a labelled 0-1000 grid → validate → refine on a zoomed crop → verify the crop alone → retry with the rejection as feedback, up to `options.max_attempts` (never more than CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS). Gated on the presence score (≥ 7) and hint presence/auto — `image sharpness` (quality) is never boxed. Model-dependent; the invariants: identical score/verdict with `boxes` off, every attempt in `localization.attempts` and in `regions` (`attrs.accepted`), `a parked car` ≤ 2 attempts, and `artifacts.attempts[n].svg` renders that attempt. Every call counts against CLASSIFIER_MAX_LLM_CALLS.
